anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$

anchor.note: Big-O notation is covered by the reader profile (asymptotic analysis).

anchor.quote: Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

anchor.note: The page only gives a range for sigma and never says what it denotes (an intermediate exponent between log_m(s/W) and lambda); earlier pages bind sigma to a row or an exponent of x, which does not apply.

gaps.note: False and inconsistent with the page: the page itself says the construction gives s<Wm, i.e. s/W<m, and the next sentence needs log_m(s/W)<1. The saving exists because s/W<m (paper lines 168, 1468, 2239). The inequality is reversed.

gaps.quote: so the internal sum is at most a constant times $f^\lambda$ for every $\lambda>0$
gaps.note: Overstated: the geometric series converges (ratio below 1) only when lambda>log_m(s/W), and the page also needs lambda>tau(1+eta/vartheta) and lambda<1. For small lambda the ratio exceeds 1 and the sum is not O(f^lambda). The paper (line 2416) uses a<m^lambda, i.e. only lambda in the stated range.

gaps.quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$
gaps.note: Does not follow: with f>=d^vartheta one only gets f^sigma d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} <= f, and for f near d^vartheta the factor d^{vartheta(1-sigma)} is about f^{1-sigma}, which exceeds f^{lambda-sigma} since lambda<1. So the bound is not O(f^lambda). The paper (lines 2421-2442) keeps the leaf bound as O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and only afterwards combines pieces into O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda'>sigma+beta(1-sigma).

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: The page never says what a kernel is (the paper's individual selected-bit C kernel applied to one chunk), nor why one kernel costs O(1) per chunk per unit volume, so the reader cannot check the leaf cost.
